title: Oracle-Robust Online Alignment for Large Language Models
claim: Our robust method trades a small nominal-fit loss for near-flat performance under oracle stress, beating the baseline past a crossover.
layout: 2 line-plot panels, left-to-right, dotted vertical line marking the crossover
description: Two side-by-side line plots share the x-axis α, which runs from 0 to 1 and interpolates from the true oracle to the worst-case oracle. The left panel plots stress loss for Nominal SAIL (blue circles) and Robust SAIL (orange squares). The blue curve rises steeply from about 0.6923 to 0.6960. The orange curve stays almost flat near 0.6931. The two curves cross at about α≈0.23, marked by a green dotted vertical line. The right panel plots the paired gap, Robust minus Nominal, as an orange line with circles. It falls linearly from about +0.0008 to −0.0028 and crosses a dashed zero line at the same green marker. The legends and titles carry the key labels. The eye goes first to the diverging curves and their crossing point.
caption: Left: true-to-worst oracle stress curve at $\rho_{\mathrm{mis}}=0.075$. Right: Robust SAIL sacrifices ideal-oracle fitting but remains nearly flat along the stress path and becomes better after $\alpha\approx0.23$.
abstract: We study online alignment of large language models under misspecified preference feedback, where the observed preference oracle deviates from an ideal but unknown ground-truth oracle. The online LLM alignment problem is a bi-level reinforcement problem due to the coupling between data collection and policy updates. Recently, the problem has been reduced to a tractable single-level objective in the SAIL (Self-Improving Efficient Online Alignment) framework. In this paper, we introduce a pointwise oracle uncertainty set in this problem and formulate an oracle-robust online alignment objective as a worst-case optimization problem. For log-linear policies, we show that this robust objective admits an exact closed-form decomposition into the original loss function plus an explicit sensitivity penalty. In the finite-response log-linear setting, we develop projected stochastic composite updates for the resulting weakly convex objective and prove $\widetilde{O}(\varepsilon^{-2})$ oracle complexity for reaching approximate stationarity.
